outcome: Since 26 January 2024 two things bearing on the bullet have appeared, neither accepted by a referee: a claimed proof for the first Weyl algebra (Zheglov, posted October 2024, v5 January 2026), and two July 2026 results that by a standard implication refute the conjecture for every Weyl algebra of rank n at least 3 (a Jacobian conjecture counterexample in three variables, announced by Levent Alpöge and credited to Claude Fable 5, with a formal check in the Archive of Formal Proofs; and an explicit non-automorphic endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra in Long's arXiv preprint 2608.23777, which credits ChatGPT 5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5). The second and first Weyl algebras remain open in the accepted literature.
problem_asks: Read from the bullet alone: every algebra endomorphism of a Weyl algebra is an automorphism. Unpacked: (1) the claim is universal over the Weyl algebras, so for each n >= 1 the Weyl algebra A_n over a field K of characteristic zero, every endomorphism of A_n is an automorphism. The bullet names no n and no field beyond 'a Weyl algebra'; the Wikipedia lead states it for the first Weyl algebra over a characteristic-zero field and gives the n-th version as the generalisation (Bass, Connell and Wright, 1982). (2) Parts that can be settled separately: DC_1 (n = 1, the original Dixmier 1968 question), DC_2 (n = 2), and DC_n for each n >= 3. (3) 'Endomorphism' is read as unital K-algebra endomorphism and 'automorphism' as bijective endomorphism. (4) The bullet does not separate the parts, so a counterexample at a single n falsifies the universal reading as stated; the bullet does not say whether it intends n = 1 alone. Both readings are recorded for the judging pass. The stable equivalence with the Jacobian conjecture (Tsuchimoto 2005; Belov-Kanel and Kontsevich 2005-2007; Adjamagbo and van den Essen 2006) is background, not part of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Bass, Connell and Wright (1982) proved that the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra implies the Jacobian conjecture in n variables (DC_n implies JC_n). Background only; recorded because it fixes the direction in which the 2026 Jacobian counterexample bears on Dixmier. Primary paper not opened; the statement is taken from secondary sources (Wikipedia Dixmier article; search summaries).
events.delivers: DC_n implies JC_n, for each n. Establishes no instance of either conjecture.
events.remains: Not applicable to the bullet's own status; the implication is what lets a JC_n failure transfer to DC_n.
events.direction: Links the two conjectures; it cuts neither way on the bullet by itself.

events.what_happened: Tsuchimoto (Osaka Journal of Mathematics, vol. 42, no. 2, June 2005) proved that the stable Dixmier and stable Jacobian conjectures are equivalent. Background; primary paper not opened, taken from the Wikipedia article and the arXiv listing of Belov-Kanel and Kontsevich, which states that the main result was already published by Tsuchimoto.
events.delivers: Stable equivalence of the Dixmier and Jacobian conjectures (all n, in the stable sense). No instance of either conjecture is settled.
events.remains: Both conjectures, in every dimension.
events.direction: Equivalence; neither way on its own.

events.what_happened: Belov-Kanel and Kontsevich, 'The Jacobian Conjecture is stably equivalent to the Dixmier Conjecture', arXiv math/0512171 (the 0512 identifier places it in December 2005; the day is not recorded here). They prove that the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra. Published Moscow Mathematical Journal 7 (2007), no. 2, 209-218 (per search summary). Abstract seen in search snippet; arXiv abstract page not opened.
events.revisions: Journal version Moscow Mathematical Journal 2007 (per search summary).
events.delivers: JC_{2n} implies DC_n, for each n; with the easy direction, stable equivalence. No instance of either conjecture is settled.
events.remains: Both conjectures in each dimension.
events.direction: Reduces the Dixmier conjecture for each n to the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n.

events.what_happened: Adjamagbo and van den Essen, 'On the equivalence of the Jacobian, Dixmier and Poisson Conjectures in any characteristic', arXiv math/0608009 (August 2006 identifier; day not recorded). Extends the equivalence to positive characteristic and includes the Poisson conjecture, giving the chain JC_{2n} implies PC_n implies DC_n implies JC_n (as quoted in a DeepMind formal-conjectures pull request). Background; arXiv abstract not opened, from search snippet.
events.delivers: Equivalence of the three conjectures in any characteristic (stable sense); no instance settled.
events.remains: All three conjectures in each dimension.
events.direction: Equivalence and the implication chain that transfers a Jacobian failure to the Dixmier problem.

events.what_happened: arXiv 1011.3009, 'An analogue of the Conjecture of Dixmier is true for the algebra of polynomial integro-differential operators' (November 2010 identifier). An analogue, not the Weyl algebra; discounted for this bullet. Abstract seen only in the search snippet; not opened. Authors not recorded from the snippet.
events.delivers: A different algebra (polynomial integro-differential operators) for which the analogous endomorphism statement holds. Says nothing about A_n.
events.remains: The bullet's Weyl-algebra statement, entirely.
events.direction: Affirmative for an analogue of the algebra, so it cuts toward the conjecture only for a different algebra.

events.what_happened: Bavula and Levandovskyy (2020), per search summaries, proved the conjecture for A_1 when P and Q are sums of at most two homogeneous elements. Pre-window partial result for n = 1; paper not opened.
events.delivers: Dixmier conjecture for A_1 restricted to pairs P, Q where P is a sum of at most two homogeneous elements (no degree restriction). A restricted case of DC_1.
events.remains: DC_1 for all other pairs; DC_n for n >= 2.
events.direction: Partial, affirmative, for n = 1 only.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2012.11659, 'The hom-associative Weyl algebras in prime characteristic' (December 2020 identifier). Per the search snippet, it gives an endomorphism of A_1 in characteristic p that is not surjective (x maps to x + x^p, y to y). That is a different question: the bullet is stated for characteristic zero. Discounted; paper not opened.
events.delivers: Non-surjective endomorphisms of the Weyl algebra in prime characteristic. Different hypothesis (characteristic p); does not touch characteristic zero.
events.remains: Everything the bullet asks for in characteristic zero.
events.direction: Counterexample in a different characteristic; cuts neither way for characteristic zero.
events.object: The map x maps to x + x^p, y maps to y on A_1 over a field of characteristic p; x^p is central, so it is an endomorphism whose image misses x (degree comparison). Explicit. Taken from the search snippet; not checked by me.

events.what_happened: Guccione, Guccione and Valqui, 'The Dixmier conjecture and the shape of possible counterexamples', arXiv 1111.6100 (v1 25 Nov 2011, v2 29 May 2012, v3 30 Oct 2013). Version v3 states B > 15, where B is the minimum over counterexamples (P, Q) of the gcd of the total degrees of P and Q. The date given is the v3 date because the B > 15 statement is confirmed only in v3; earlier versions not checked. Pre-window.
events.revisions: v1 2011-11-25; v2 2012-05-29; v3 2013-10-30 (the B > 15 statement is confirmed in v3; v1 and v2 not checked for it).
events.delivers: Lower bound on the size of any counterexample: gcd of total degrees greater than 15. Restricts what a counterexample could look like; settles no instance of DC_n.
events.remains: DC_n for every n, including whether any counterexample exists.
events.direction: Constrains a hypothetical counterexample; cuts toward the conjecture only in the sense of bounding where a counterexample could be.

events.remains: DC_1 in general; DC_n for n >= 2.
events.direction: Partial, affirmative, for n = 1 only, scope not read.

events.what_happened: Guccione, Guccione and Valqui, 'Number of homogeneous components of counterexamples to the Dixmier conjecture', arXiv 2402.11135, first posted 16 February 2024 (v1 only). Inside the window. Proves: if P is a sum of at most four homogeneous elements of A_1 and [P, Q] = 1, then P and Q generate A_1. Generalises arXiv 2210.00257. Published Communications in Algebra 53(3) (2025), pp. 1307-1319, DOI 10.1080/00927872.2024.2407991 (from search summary; the journal page not opened).
events.revisions: v1 16 Feb 2024 only (per arXiv listing). Journal version Communications in Algebra 2025 (per search summary).
events.delivers: DC_1 restricted to pairs (P, Q) where P is a sum of at most four homogeneous elements of A_1 (over a field of characteristic zero, per the abstract). Restricts the counterexample shape; settles no full instance.
events.remains: DC_1 for all other pairs; DC_n for n >= 2.

events.what_happened: Alexander Zheglov, 'The Conjecture of Dixmier for the first Weyl algebra is true', arXiv 2410.06959 (math.RA), first posted 9 October 2024. Claims a full proof that every algebra endomorphism of A_1 over a field K of characteristic zero is an automorphism. Versions: v2 14 Oct 2024; v3 23 Oct 2024; v4 17 Feb 2025 (adds an investigation of solutions to the string equation); v5 19 Jan 2026 (current; 78 pages; extends introduction and simplifies calculations at the last stage of the proof). Zheglov also gave a seminar talk on the proof in Moscow on 12 May 2025 (per search summary; abstract seen only in snippet). Proof sketch per the seminar abstract: normal forms for ordinary differential operators, Newton polygons, the string equation [P, Q] = 1. No journal publication, referee report, or correction is named on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Claims DC_1 in full: every endomorphism of A_1 over a characteristic-zero field is an automorphism. The claimed scope is n = 1 only.
events.remains: Per the claim itself nothing; for the bullet's other parts, DC_2 and DC_n for n >= 3 are not addressed by this preprint.
events.time_since_posted: about 24 months (about 9 months since the last revision)
events.doubts: No specific error identified in any source I opened. Doubt rests on the record: the preprint is single-authored and unrefereed; I found no journal publication or referee report. The Wikipedia Dixmier article calls it 'a proposed proof', does not treat DC_1 as settled, and says DC_1 remains open. A 2025 survey on skew PBW extensions describes Zheglov as claiming DC_1, using 'claims' (per a search summary; that survey not opened). No expert verification or refutation found in any search.
events.direction: Affirmative for n = 1: every endomorphism of A_1 is an automorphism.

events.what_happened: Junhu Guo and Alexander Zheglov, Mathematical Notes (Matematicheskie Zametki) vol. 116, issue 2 (2024), per search summary. Two conditional results on the first Weyl algebra: (a) the Dixmier conjecture holds if a certain polynomial equation has a nontrivial commuting solution whose solutions split into finitely many Aut(A_1)-orbits; (b) endomorphisms of 'monomial type' have no nontrivial fixed points. Month not recorded. The mathnet page could not be reached (connection refused), so this is from search snippets only.
events.delivers: Conditional on a finiteness hypothesis on solutions of a polynomial equation, DC_1 holds. Not an unconditional result.
events.remains: Unconditional DC_1; DC_2 and higher.

events.what_happened: Van Hoang Dinh (Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Education, per the journal front matter, not 'Dinh Nguyen' as first searched), 'A Computational Approach to Examining Dixmier Conjecture in a Specific Case', Journal of Technical Education Science. Journal record: revised 03/07/2025, accepted 17/07/2025, online first 04/05/2026 (day/month order is not clear from the page; 4 May 2026 read as day-first). events.what_happened: William Fajardo and Oswaldo Lezama, 'The Dixmier problem for skew PBW extensions and rings', arXiv 2506.09285, v1 10 June 2025 (v2 30 Jun, v3 1 Jul, v4 4 Aug, v5 21 Dec 2025). Introduces Dixmier algebras for skew PBW extensions; computes concrete nontrivial automorphisms of A_1(K); conjectures that CSD_n(K) is Dixmier when n is even. Analogue, discounted for this bullet: it treats skew PBW extensions and does not claim to resolve the Weyl-algebra question.

events.direction: Analogue; does not decide the bullet either way.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge announced on X an explicit polynomial map F: C^3 to C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant -2 that is not injective, so it has no polynomial inverse; this refutes the Jacobian conjecture in dimension three. The post was not retrieved (HTTP 402 when fetched). Date: 19 July 2026 in US time, about 02:19 UTC on 20 July (search summaries); Wikipedia and the Gao paper say 19 July, the Archive of Formal Proofs and several news items say 20 July. No arXiv preprint by Alpöge was found; a later paper's reference list is reported to say the item will be updated to a preprint when one appears (search summary; that paper not identified). Tao's blog states the result as Theorem 2 (21 July 2026). Sources differ on whether the post thanks Akhil Mathew and Claude Fable 5 (see disputes). Dixmier is not mentioned in any source for this event except Wikipedia's Dixmier article, which derives DC_n false for n > 2 from the implications. The bullet's consequence therefore rests on the implication DC_n implies JC_n (Bass, Connell and Wright 1982), not on any statement by the announcer.
events.revisions: No revision found; no preprint found.
events.delivers: Jacobian conjecture false in dimension three over Q (and over C), since the map is defined over Q with three rational points sharing an image. Identity-padding (AFP entry) gives JC_n false for every n >= 3. Through DC_n implies JC_n, the Dixmier conjecture is false for every n >= 3 (the implication is what Wikipedia's Dixmier article cites). Does not address DC_1 or DC_2, and does not address JC_2.
events.remains: DC_1 and DC_2 (not addressed); JC_2 (open, stated by Tao and the AFP entry); the event does not write out an explicit Weyl-algebra endomorphism for A_3 (Long's paper says it can be obtained through the standard Jacobian-to-Weyl lift, not explicit).

checked_by.qualification: Professor of mathematics; a leading expert in algebraic geometry and related areas.
checked_by.what_they_did: Blog digestion of the counterexample, 21 July 2026: states the map (Equation 1) and Theorem 2 (non-zero constant Jacobian, not invertible), and explains the geometric mechanism. The post itself reports that he used an AI chatbot to confirm several calculations.

checked_by.who: Arno van den Essen (single author per the arXiv abstract page)
checked_by.qualification: Expert in polynomial automorphisms and the Jacobian conjecture (the paper is in that area).
checked_by.what_they_did: Abstract states that the paper gives an elementary derivation of a counterexample which is, apart from linear coordinate changes, the example found by Alpöge. This is a re-derivation rather than a verification of the announced map.

events.directly_checkable: Yes. The map is explicit (Tao, Equation 1). The Jacobian determinant is a fixed polynomial identity, and three distinct rational points share one image; both can be checked by computer algebra or by hand.
events.doubts: None found on the mathematics. Record-level doubts only: (a) no preprint or journal version by the announcer; (b) the announcement date is 19 July (US time) or 20 July (UTC), depending on source; (c) affiliation reported as Anthropic in some coverage and Harvard in others (search snippets, unopened); (d) the post text is disputed: Long's paper says it thanks Akhil Mathew and Fable, while the phys.org article quotes the post as 'hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx' with no thanks.
events.direction: Cuts against the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 3 and, via DC_n implies JC_n, against the Dixmier conjecture for every n >= 3 (the chain is stated by Wikipedia's Dixmier article, not by the announcer or by Tao).
events.object: A polynomial map F: C^3 to C^3 of degree seven (Tao's Equation 1): F(z1, z2, z3) = ((1+z1z2)^3 z3 + z2^2(1+z1z2)(4+3z1z2), z2 + 3z1(1+z1z2)^2 z3 + 3z1z2^2(4+3z1z2), 2z1 - 3z1^2 z2 - z1^3 z3). Its Jacobian determinant is the constant -2, so it is a Keller map that is locally invertible everywhere, yet three distinct rational points (per search summaries of MathWorld and the AFP entry, not checked against those pages: (0,0,-1/4), (1,-3/2,13/2), (-1,3/2,13/2)) map to (-1/4,0,0). It is explicit, not a non-constructive existence proof. One aggregator lists the first point with a sign difference; the Tao formula is taken as the reference.
people: Akhil Mathew (credited with suggesting the problem, per Long's paper and secondary coverage)
Terence Tao (exposition; verification of the identities per search summary)

Other sources name it 'Fable' (Tao: 'the Fable AI') or 'Claude Fable 5' (news). Prompting details are not public (phys.org, quoting coverage). events.what_happened: Arthur Freitas Ramos, David Barros Hulak and Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz, 'Formal Verification of an Explicit Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture', Archive of Formal Proofs, dated 20 July 2026 (PDF outline dated 21 July). An Isabelle/HOL formalisation that checks the Jacobian entries equal the complex partial derivatives, the determinant is identically -2, and three distinct rational points share an image, so the map has no polynomial inverse. Identity-padding gives counterexamples in every dimension at least 3. Makes no claim about dimension two. Does not mention the Dixmier conjecture or Weyl algebras (checked on the page). It formalises the Alpöge map; it is a machine check of event alpoge-2026-jc3-announcement, not an independent result.
events.revisions: Entry date 20 July 2026; PDF outline 21 July 2026.
events.delivers: Formal, machine-checked: JC_3 fails for the explicit map; JC_n fails for n >= 3 by padding. Nothing about Weyl algebras.
events.remains: DC_1 and DC_2; JC_2; the Weyl-algebra endomorphism for DC_n, n >= 3, is not formalised in this entry.

checked_by.what_they_did: Formal Isabelle/HOL verification of the explicit map and its non-invertibility. The entry states: 'AI assistance was used for proof engineering' and 'The final definitions, statements, and proofs are checked by Isabelle.'

Its text credits Alpöge (19 July), Gallagher (20 July) and Speyer (23 July). No sentence mentions Dixmier or Weyl algebras (abstract page read; full text not read).

Abstract page read; full text not read. No mention of Dixmier, Weyl algebras, Claude or AI in the abstract page.

events.what_happened: Christopher D. Long, 'An Explicit Counterexample to the Rank-Two Poisson Conjecture', arXiv 2608.23777 (math.RA, math.AG). Submitted 22 July 2026 (v1; the only version listed). Main result: an explicit Poisson endomorphism of a four-variable polynomial algebra with two canonical pairs (R = x(2 - 3xq), and polynomials T, D, S), which disproves the rank-two Poisson conjecture (PC_2). Appendix B: 'the same four output polynomials and their Hamiltonian duals' give an explicit endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra over C that is not an automorphism; the paper states 'Consequently, DC(4) is false.' The appendix also says the same endomorphism 'can also be obtained from the announced three-variable Keller map through the standard Jacobian-to-Weyl lift', i.e. the paper points to the Alpöge map for rank 3. The arXiv identifier prefix 2608 (August) does not match the stated 22 July date; the date is taken from the arXiv page. The AI statements are from the full HTML text of v1, read through a fetch tool that quotes with a small model, so the wording should be checked against the HTML. MathWorld's Dixmier entry describes the same appendix (Long 2026, 22 Jul 2026, 'developed with AI assistance and checked by its author'). The arXiv abstract page itself does not mention AI.
events.revisions: v1 22 Jul 2026 only (per arXiv abstract page). Identifier prefix 2608 is inconsistent with the 22 July date; not resolved.
events.delivers: Poisson: PC_2 false (rank-two Poisson conjecture, two canonical pairs). Dixmier: explicit non-automorphic endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra over C, so DC(4) is false per the paper; by adjoining unchanged generators, DC(n) for every n >= 4 (per MathWorld's statement of the same construction). The paper also points to DC(3) via the lift from the Alpöge map (stated as obtainable, not written out). Does not settle DC_1 or DC_2 (the chain PC_n implies DC_n implies JC_n only propagates falsity upward, so a Poisson counterexample in rank 2 does not disprove DC_2).
events.remains: DC_1 and DC_2 (open; not addressed by the endomorphism); DC_3 rests on the lift from the Alpöge map rather than an explicit A_3 formula in this paper; full paper-level formalisation incomplete (see doubts).

events.direction: Cuts against the fourth-rank Dixmier conjecture (DC(4) false over C), and, by adjoining generators, DC(n) for n >= 4; cuts against the rank-two Poisson conjecture; neutral on DC_1 and DC_2.
events.object: Explicit polynomials R, T, D, S in C[x, q, p, z], with R = x(2 - 3xq), satisfying the required Poisson relations, giving a Poisson endomorphism of the rank-two algebra with Jacobian determinant 1, preserving the symplectic form, with a fibre of exactly three points (Poisson counterexample). Appendix B: the endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra A_4 over C given by X_i to f_i (f = (R, T, D, S)) and d_1 to H_D, d_2 to H_S, d_3 to -H_R, d_4 to -H_T, where H_F is the Hamiltonian derivation of F. Non-automorphy: the author argues that an automorphism would force the image to be all of C[f_1..f_4] (surjectivity), contradicting Proposition 7.1. This is an explicit map with a constructive proof, per the paper's own description; the argument was read from the HTML summary, not checked.

Appendix B's endomorphism uses the same four output polynomials and Hamiltonian duals, so the system's construction is load-bearing for the A_4 result.

events.what_happened: A pull request to google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, PR #4491 'feat(Arxiv): add the Weyl algebra and the Dixmier conjecture (math/0608009)' by user korbonits, opened 21 July 2026. Adds Lean statements of the Dixmier family: dixmier_conjecture (the family over all n, marked as false in the PR description), variants.dimension_one (DC_1, open) and variants.dimension_two (DC_2, open), and completes the chain JC_{2n} implies PC_n implies DC_n implies JC_n. A later update in the PR says PC_2 is false and that the chain propagates falsity upward, so DC_1 and DC_2 stay open. A formal statement and a status label, not a proof; recorded because it is a project-level classification of the bullet's status made from the same events.
events.revisions: Opened 21 July 2026; later update in the same PR (date not recorded).
events.delivers: Formal statements of the Dixmier family and its variants; status labels only. Does not establish any instance.
events.remains: Not applicable; the PR records DC_1 and DC_2 as open.
events.doubts: The status labels are the author's and are not reviewed. The PR description reads the chain as propagating falsity upward; that is the logic recorded in direction.

disputes.summary: Credit for the three-variable Jacobian counterexample: Alpöge announced it; the AFP entry (authors' account) and Long's paper credit Claude Fable (or Fable) with the work leading to the map; Long's paper says the post thanks Akhil Mathew for asking about the problem and Fable for working on it. A phys.org article quotes the post as 'hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx' with no thanks. Alpöge's own text was not retrieved (HTTP 402), so the wording of the post is unresolved.

Announcement date of the three-variable Jacobian counterexample: 19 July 2026 per Wikipedia's Jacobian and Dixmier articles and Gao's paper; 20 July per the AFP entry, Tao's coverage and several news items. The post appears to be about 02:19 UTC on 20 July, which is the evening of 19 July in US time zones. The record uses 19 July (US time) with this note.

Status of DC_1: Zheglov's 2024 preprint (v5 January 2026) claims a full proof; the Wikipedia Dixmier article calls it 'a proposed proof' and says DC_1 remains open; the JTE paper (Dinh, 2026) and search snippets of later surveys describe DC_1 as open. No referee report or journal acceptance of the Zheglov proof was found.

Status of the fourth-rank Weyl endomorphism (Long): the arXiv paper's Appendix B and the README say it is constructed and proved non-automorphic (Lean coverage of the Weyl part claimed); pull request #2 (17 Sep 2026) says the actual Weyl-algebra endomorphism is further work. MathWorld reports no independent external verification as of 7 Sep 2026. These statements conflict and were not resolved.

arXiv 2608.23777 carries an August-2026 identifier prefix, but the arXiv page gives submission on 22 July 2026. Not resolved from the sources opened; the judging pass may want to check the arXiv listing history.

summary: Dixmier's question (1968) asks whether every endomorphism of a Weyl algebra over a characteristic-zero field is an automorphism. The record below separates three layers. (1) Background, all pre-window: Bass, Connell and Wright (1982) gave DC_n implies JC_n; Tsuchimoto (2005) and Belov-Kanel and Kontsevich (arXiv math/0512171, Dec 2005) gave stable equivalence of the Dixmier and Jacobian conjectures; Adjamagbo and van den Essen (2006) extended this to any characteristic and added the Poisson conjecture; Guccione, Guccione and Valqui (arXiv 1111.6100, v3 Oct 2013) bounded the gcd of total degrees of any counterexample by B > 15. (2) Inside the window, for the first Weyl algebra only: Guccione et al. (arXiv 2402.11135, 16 Feb 2024, in Communications in Algebra 2025) proved DC_1 when P is a sum of at most four homogeneous elements; Guo and Zheglov (Mathematical Notes 2024, conditional); Zheglov (arXiv 2410.06959, 9 Oct 2024, v5 19 Jan 2026) claims the full DC_1, unrefereed and with no acceptance found; Dinh (JTE, 2026) checks degrees (6, 9) only; Fajardo and Lezama (arXiv 2506.09285, 2025) is an analogue for skew PBW extensions. (3) July 2026, bearing on n >= 3: Alpöge announced (19 July, US time) an explicit degree-seven polynomial map on C^3 with constant Jacobian -2 that is not injective, refuting the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 3. Tao's exposition (21 July) and an Isabelle/HOL entry in the Archive of Formal Proofs (20 July; accepted AFP entry, sorry-freeness not separately checked) confirm it. None of the Alpöge-side sources mentions Dixmier. The Dixmier consequence follows from the implication DC_n implies JC_n (Bass, Connell and Wright), which Wikipedia's Dixmier article applies to say DC_n and PC_n are false for every n > 2 and open for n = 1, 2. Long (arXiv 2608.23777, submitted 22 July 2026, single version) gives an explicit non-automorphic endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra over C, stated in its Appendix B as 'Consequently, DC(4) is false', built from the same four polynomials as its Poisson counterexample; it also says DC(3) follows from the Alpöge map through the Jacobian-to-Weyl lift. The AI record: Alpöge's map is credited to Claude Fable 5 by the AFP authors and by Long, and the announcer's own text (X post) could not be retrieved, so the credit rests on secondary and third-party wording; Long's construction is credited by its own paper to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol ('produced during an interactive research session'), with Claude Fable 5 supplying audits and editorial comments. Tao's post states an unnamed 'AI chatbot' was used to confirm calculations; because it is unnamed, it is not in any systems list. The AFP entry's proof-engineering assistance is also unnamed. Close calls: (a) whether the bullet is read for every n (then the bullet is false from n = 3 on, by the chain plus Long's explicit A_4) or only for the first Weyl algebra (then nothing in 2026 touches it, and the only claim is Zheglov's unrefereed one); (b) whether the Alpöge result counts for DC_n given that its sources do not state the Dixmier consequence, and whether Long's explicit A_4 endomorphism, which is unrefereed and has conflicting Lean status, should be the event the bullet's status rests on; (c) the Alpöge announcement's date and the wording of the post are disputed in the sources.
competing_reading: The bullet is about 'a Weyl algebra', and Wikipedia's lead frames the original question for the first Weyl algebra. On that reading nothing bearing on the bullet was settled by an accepted argument in the window: the only claim for n = 1 (Zheglov, 2024) is unrefereed, the 2026 results are about n >= 3 and n = 4, and the bullet's status is 'open, with a claimed proof for the first case'. The opposite reading is that the bullet is universal over all Weyl algebras, so a counterexample at n = 3 or n = 4 falsifies it. Under that reading the Alpöge map plus the standard implication already disposes of the bullet for n >= 3, and Long supplies an explicit A_4 endomorphism. A further reading treats the Alpöge event as a Jacobian result that the Dixmier bullet only inherits through a theorem nobody in the 2026 sources states, so that Long's explicit endomorphism is the only Weyl-algebra object exhibited; that reading also weighs Long's unrefereed status and conflicting Lean coverage.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Alpöge's X post and any preprint by him, and the Zenodo Lean record reported in a secondary source (not opened). (2) A direct statement or written-out formula for an endomorphism of A_3 obtained from the Alpöge map by the Jacobian-to-Weyl lift, checked by computer algebra; or an independent check of Long's Appendix B formulas and non-surjectivity. (3) A Lean build of the Weyl endomorphism itself, resolving the README versus pull request #2 conflict. (4) A referee report or journal acceptance for Zheglov's proof of DC_1, or a published error in it; and for Long's paper and the Alpöge announcement, a refereed publication. (5) The primary text of Bass, Connell and Wright (1982) and of Tsuchimoto (2005), to confirm the direction and scope of the implications the record depends on. (6) The date of arXiv 2608.23777 from the arXiv listing history, resolving the identifier mismatch.
